标题: HarnessX: A Composable, Adaptive, and Evolvable Agent Harness Foundry
S2_TLDR: HarnessX, a foundry for composable, adaptive, and evolvable agent harnesses, is introduced, suggesting that agent progress need not come from model scaling alone: composing and evolving runtime interfaces from execution feedback is an actionable and complementary lever.

标题: Harness-R1: Learning to Edit Executable Runtime Harnesses from Agent Failure Trajectories
S2_TLDR: This work introduces Harness-R1, the first method, to the authors' knowledge, that makes failure-conditioned, lifecycle-wide editing of an existing executable runtime a learned capability, and post-trains a dedicated harness engineer with online reinforcement learning so that its edits are optimized for the realized task success they produce.

标题: HarnessBank: Semantic Gene-Bank Search with Gated Verification for Agent-Harness Self-Evolution
S2_TLDR: HarnessBank is introduced, a trustworthy agent-harness self-evolution framework that pairs a task agent with a separate evolver agent for iterative failure diagnosis, harness generation, and evolution verification and maintains a Harness Gene Bank composed of high-performing harnesses of different semantic coordinates.

标题: Hierarchical Self-Improvement: A Framework for Task-Specific Evolvable Agent Harnesses
S2_TLDR: Results demonstrate task-specific harness evolution as a viable axis for improving frozen LLM agents under clear empirical limits.

标题: Self-Evolving Coding Agents
S2_TLDR: This survey aims to clarify the conceptual boundaries of self-evolving coding agents and provide a foundation for designing more adaptive, reliable, and software-aware agentic systems.

标题: MUSE: A Unified Agentic Harness for MLLMs
S2_TLDR: MUSE is introduced, a multimodal unified structured execution harness that wraps any off-the-shelf MLLM with composable modules for task representation, visual processing, perception tool use, structured parsing, deterministic verification, and verifier-guided repair, without any model retraining.

标题: SHarP: Saliency-based Pruning of Agent Harnesses
S2_TLDR: This paper proposes SHarP (Saliency-based Harness Pruning), a simple yet effective pruning strategy based on the saliency of each harness module with respect to performance and efficiency, which provides new perspectives on agent harness design and optimization.

标题: FreeEvolve: Learning to Evolve Beyond Fixed Loops
S2_TLDR: FREEEVOLVE automates the evolution campaign by itself, yet improves the primary held-out metric by 13.6 points on average and matches or exceeds hand-designed evolvers, demonstrating transferability across environments.

标题: Self-Evolving Coding Agents
Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves
S2_TLDR: Self-Harness is introduced, a new paradigm in which an LLM-based agent improves its own operating harness, without relying on human engineers or stronger external agents, and is suggested a path toward LLM-based agents that are not merely shaped by their harnesses, but can also participate in reshaping them.

标题: Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents
S2_TLDR: The evaluation of automatic harness evolution procedures is revisited and the need for matched-budget baselines and held-out evaluation to distinguish genuine harness improvements from benchmark-specific search and overfitting is highlighted.

标题: Adapting the Interface, Not the Model: Runtime Harness Adaptation for Deterministic LLM Agents
S2_TLDR: Life-Harness is proposed, a lifecycle-aware runtime harness that improves frozen LLM agents without changing model weights or evaluation environments, and results position runtime interface adaptation as a complementary alternative to model-centric agent training.

标题: From Failed Trajectories to Reliable LLM Agents: Diagnosing and Repairing Harness Flaws
S2_TLDR: This paper proposes HarnessFix, a trace-grounded and diagnosis-driven framework for repairing agent harnesses, and shows that it improves the performance over the initial harnesses by 6.3% to 18.4%, significantly outperforming human-designed and self-evolution baselines.

标题: HarnessCompass: Guiding Automatic Harness Evolution toward Generalizable and Effective Agent Harnesses
S2_TLDR: HarnessCompass is proposed, a novel automatic harness evolution framework built around constrained evolution, proactive feedback, and component-wise optimization that improves Pass@1 from 54\% to 66\% in only 5 evolution iterations, outperforming AHE in both effectiveness and evolution efficiency.

标题: Co-Harness: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Model Weights for LLM Agents
S2_TLDR: Co-Harness is introduced, a framework that jointly optimizes the agent harness and model parameters during post-training and suggests that joint harness and model optimization is an effective way to improve agents beyond fixed-harness post-training.

标题: AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces
S2_TLDR: The proposed AutoSaddler, an automatic harness optimization framework that formulates harness improvement as an offline learning problem and iteratively updates the harness using failure signals from mini-batches, suggests that automatic harness optimization is a promising path toward more performant and reliable agent systems.

标题: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
S2_TLDR: To the authors' knowledge, JIT-Agent is the first model purpose-built for just-in-time harness generation, establishing harness intelligence as a trainable, transferable, and compounding dimension of agent capability orthogonal to model scaling.

标题: Stop Comparing LLM Agents Without Disclosing the Harness
Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification
S2_TLDR: HarnessLens is introduced, a budget-aware framework for automated harness evolution that jointly explores the task space and user-configurable components, derives candidate modifications from execution trajectories, and selectively verifies each candidate on behavior-relevant tasks using an attributable-evidence gate.

标题: WHALE: A Simple Recipe for Joint Harness-Weight Optimization
S2_TLDR: Weight-Harness Alternating LEarning (WHALE), a simple recipe that alternates two phases: updating the model under the current harness, then searching for a better harness under the updated model with online rejection-sampling fine-tuning and Meta-Harness, is proposed.

标题: ModularRSI: Modular and Generalizable Recursive Harness Self-Improvement
S2_TLDR: ModularRSI is proposed, a benchmark-disjoint, contrastive, and modular framework for generalizable harness evolution that contrasts successful and failed trajectories for the same task and aggregates evidence across tasks to identify recurring behavioral deficiencies.

标题: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
S2_TLDR: It is found that generated harnesses remain substantially behind mature human-engineered references on code and on search and research, while matching or exceeding the selected references on writing and machine-learning experimentation, with large variation in execution cost.

标题: The Interplay of Harness Design and Post-Training in LLM Agents
S2_TLDR: It is shown that harness-aware post-training not only improves in-distribution performance but also enables agents to robustly adapt to OOD settings, highlighting the importance of harness-aware post-training under such shifts.

标题: Better Harnesses, Smaller Models: Building 90% Cheaper Agents via Automated Harness Adaptation
S2_TLDR: This work creates a framework that maps agent failure modes to harness adaptation strategies, and builds a harness optimizer that automatically discovers effective adaptations from failure trajectories, suggesting that harness adaptation can expand the practical deployment range of SLM agents in routine business tasks.

标题: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
S2_TLDR: This work evaluates 5 frontier LLMs as optimizers both under a shared coding harness and under their native harnesses across 4 downstream tasks, and establishes harness optimization as a measurable and discriminative capability with large space for improvement.

标题: Task-CoEvolve: Efficient Harness Optimization via Adaptive Validation Task Selection
S2_TLDR: Task-CoEvolve builds on the observation that tasks on which candidate harnesses disagree are more informative for distinguishing among them than tasks that are consistently solved or failed, and uses variance-weighted sampling based on past outcomes to focus evaluation on tasks near the capability frontier.

标题: EvoTrainer: Co-Evolving LLM Policies and Training Harnesses for Autonomous Agentic Reinforcement Learning
S2_TLDR: EvoTrainer is introduced, an autonomous training framework that co-evolves LLM policies and training-side harnesses through empirical feedback: it diagnoses rollout-level evidence, revises diagnostics, backtests interventions, and accumulates reusable skills.

标题: AutoDesign: Meta-Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Design
S2_TLDR: This paper presents AutoDesign, a framework that aligns with human design priors, where a meta-harness optimizer guides a code agent to recursively improve harness based on rollout feedback, and introduces PosterBench, comprising a 100-paper Main Track spanning five disciplines and PosterBench-mini, a shared 10-paper subset for controlled evaluation.

标题: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
S2_TLDR: WikiSkill is introduced, a framework that co-evolves agent skills with a persistent knowledge base (wiki) and it is found that skill evolution complements model scaling: larger models generally benefit more from evolved skills, while smaller models with skills can outperform substantially larger models without them.

标题: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models: On-Policy Correction Helps Weaker Models Catch Up Where Imitation Fails
S2_TLDR: An on-policy expert-correction pipeline is developed, automated by a meta-level MLE agent, that localizes the failing turn in the weaker model's own rollout and asks the expert to rewrite only that turn, which preserves the model's planning style and combines the gains of harness evolution and model adaptation.

标题: From Question Answering to Task Completion: A Survey on Agent System and Harness Design
S2_TLDR: This survey argues that agent quality -- including success, efficiency, safety, and generalization -- emerges from the interaction between model capability, runtime infrastructure, task structure, and evaluation design.

标题: SkillOpt-Lite: Better and Faster Agent Self-evolution via One Line of Vibe
S2_TLDR: This work formalizes skill optimization via Zeroth-Order (ZO) optimization, mapping classical counterparts (central difference, trust regions) to recent literature to establish three principles for convergence and generalization: file-system-based trajectory exploration, consensus attribute mining, and independent validation gating.

标题: Automated Discovery Has No Universally Superior Harness
S2_TLDR: This work systematically decomposes OpenEvolve-style evolutionary search and the TTT-Discover search harness into its constituent components and systematically evaluates 30 budget-matched harnesses across 12 model-problem pairs using more than 3.1 million LLM rollouts and repeated-trial statistical analysis, showing that discovery harnesses have a generalization problem.

标题: SoL-Pi: Recursively Scaling Auto-Research Loops for Efficient Agent Harness
S2_TLDR: This work takes an RSI-inspired approach at the harness layer, scaling auto-research loops across increasingly numerous and diverse environments for harness rollouts, and yields reusable improvements that transfer beyond their development setting.

标题: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness
S2_TLDR: This work introduces Harness-Zero, which enables harness distillation through agent-as-harness, and shows that for frontier LLMs using the same evolved harness, agent-as-harness outperforms code-as-harness.

标题: Toward Generalist Autonomous Research via Hypothesis-Tree Refinement
S2_TLDR: This work introduces Arbor, a general framework for autonomous research that combines a long-lived coordinator, short-lived executors, and Hypothesis Tree Refinement (HTR), a persistent tree that links hypotheses, artifacts, evidence, and distilled insights across time.

标题: RHO: Your Coding Agent is Secretly a Roboticist
S2_TLDR: Robotics Harness Optimization is introduced, a novel paradigm in which tool-enabled coding agents, at training time, propose and search for interpretable, neurosymbolic multi-file policy repositories (Repositories-as-Policies) that compose these primitives rather than a single prompt, function, or file.

标题: Phantom Guardrails: When Self-Improving Agent Harnesses Fix Failures That Never Happened
S2_TLDR: This work introduces the Counterfactual Fabrication Lab, a deterministic micro-lab where the correct action is known: do nothing, and presents the Counterfactual Fabrication Lab for measuring fabricated failures in self-improving agent harnesses.

标题: PILOT in the Loop: Live Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Agents
S2_TLDR: PILOT is presented, a supervisor-worker harness for live self-improvement through two coupled mechanisms: (1) live steering lets a separate supervisor redirect or abort the active worker during execution; and (2) live self-evolution distils procedures and failure modes revealed during execution into reusable skills and memory.

标题: EvoSafeHarness: Evolving Model- and Domain-Specific Harnesses for Securing Agents
S2_TLDR: EvoSafeHarness is a safety-specific optimization framework that synthesizes a deployable harness for a frozen model in a target domain, guided by model behavior, domain specifications, and fresh-context adversarial review to reject benchmark-specific rules.

标题: MetaRSI / RSI2: A Meta-Recursive Self-Improving System for Recursive Self-Improving Systems Themselves
S2_TLDR: This work argues RSI must next operate across real, diverse scientific, engineering, and meta-scientific domains, not where formal evaluation is merely tractable, and presents MetaRSI-v1, where improvement is the scheduled composition of three typed operators over one unified paradigm.

标题: LemonHarness Technical Report
S2_TLDR: The results suggest that a unified runtime boundary, callable rule knowledge, and time-aware execution can improve the stability of long-horizon agent execution.

标题: AgentStream: How Well Do Self-Evolving LLM Agents Perform Under Streaming Tasks?
S2_TLDR: AgentStream is introduced, a unified framework that evaluates self-evolving agents spanning diverse evolution components by organizing agentic benchmarks into a configurable task stream and instantiating the \texttt{Isolated}, \texttt{Sequential}, and \texttt{Interleaved} streaming scenarios at test time, which progressively vary the scope and domain composition of the stream.

标题: ADIAS: Automated Design of Interactive Agentic Systems
StateM: Reaching 95.3% Raw Accuracy, or a \$15 Frontier Run, on Terminal-Bench 2.1 via Harness Scaling
S2_TLDR: StateM is introduced, an agent-native runtime that organizes execution around durable states, phase-local context, checked transitions, recoverable runbooks, and versioned procedural practices that agents and users can inspect together to bet on harness scaling to improve the execution system around an agent without changing its model weights.

标题: Agents in the Large: Perception-Centered Architecture for Persistent Agents
S2_TLDR: Pera describes a persistent agent organized around perception and control components that continually perceive service-relevant signals from episodic task executions, internal context, and changes in the surrounding environment, and use these signals to construct lifecycle tasks.

标题: LiteEvo: Automated, Cost-Efficient Harness Evolution for Generalization to Unseen Tasks
S2_TLDR: LiteEvo is proposed, a lightweight harness-evolution algorithm whose tool-free meta-agents mine agent trajectories for reusable components, curate them into a versioned library, and compose each round's harness from it, starting every benchmark from the same neutral harness and never naming the benchmark.

标题: CogOmniControl: Reasoning-Driven Controllable Video Generation via Creative Intent Cognition
S2_TLDR: This work presents CogOmniControl, a reasoning-driven framework that factorizes controllable video generation into creative intent cognition and generation and integrates CogVLM's robust capability in guiding video generation into a closed-loop"harness-like"architecture.

标题: Statistical Priors for Implicit Preferences: Decoupling Skill Selection as a Local Harness in Personal Agents
S2_TLDR: A novel architecture that strictly decouples statistical preference learning from semantic intent parsing is explored, which achieves the lowest cumulative regret and highest test accuracy, significantly outperforming traditional memory-augmented agents.

标题: Auto-Configuring Scientific Simulators with Lightweight Coding-Agent Adapters
S2_TLDR: SIGA is introduced, a coding-agent adapter that supplies this contract through retrieval, procedural memory, agent-callable validation, and validation-gated termination while leaving the model and loop frozen.

标题: From Prompts to Contracts: Harness Engineering for Auditable Enterprise LLM Agents
S2_TLDR: A reusable engineering pattern for turning exploratory prototypes into auditable applications with versioned source, control, and validation artifacts is presented, which reconstructs this pattern into a traceable, auditable LLM-agent architecture.

标题: Who&When Pro: Can LLMs Really Attribute Failures in AI Agents?
S2_TLDR: Who&When Pro, a large-scale benchmark for automated failure attribution in agentic systems, is introduced, revealing systematic patterns in how models attribute failures across modalities, protocols, and model families and providing empirical guidance for future automated failure attribution systems.

标题: ToFu: A White-Box, Token-Efficient Agent Harness for Researchers
S2_TLDR: ToFu is presented, an agentic harness for researchers that reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands, and integrates with your development tools and provides a white-box agentic harness that allows researchers to inspect, modify, and evaluate its orchestration logic, tool-use behavior, and harness design.

标题: MDArena: Evaluating Coding Agents on Realistic Molecular Dynamics Workflows
S2_TLDR: MDArena is introduced, a benchmark of 50 containerized tasks drawn from active biomolecular simulation projects, spanning 29 molecular systems and 14 broad research protocols, including trajectory analysis, complex system preparation, free-energy protocols, and enhanced sampling, indicating that agents frequently make meaningful partial progress but fail on the fine-grained details required for reproducible scientific workflows.

标题: MetaCaster: Meta-Harness-Optimized Agent for End-to-End Few-Shot Learning of Lightweight Time Series Forecasters
S2_TLDR: This work proposes MetaCaster, a meta-harness-optimized multi-agent framework that uses agentic data generation to automatically train specialized lightweight forecasters from only a few examples and textual contexts and highlights a new TSF paradigm in which agents act not as forecasters but as intermediary engineers that prepare efficient, task-specific forecasters for deployment.

标题: SpatialGuard: Harness-Guided Verifiable Spatial Reasoning for Text-to-Image Generation
S2_TLDR: Comprehensive experiments show that SpatialGuard achieves state-of-the-art performance in complex 3D spatial layout generation and improves spatial faithfulness over existing text-to-image and layout control baselines.

标题: Dalek: A Constructive Agent Machine
Bad Genius: Counterfactual-Guided Harness Evolution Beyond Task-Specific Shortcuts
S2_TLDR: This work introduces Counterfactual Harness Search and Evolution (CHASE), which casts harness evolution as constraint generation over valid counterfactual benchmarks and formalizes an ideal shortcut-neutralized benchmark $B_0$ and establishes theoretical guarantees linking finite counterfactual archives to $B_0$ and characterizing sequential Challenger search.

标题: Mara Chain: Rethinking Failure as a Stepping Stone for AI System Auto-Evolution
S2_TLDR: Mara Chain is introduced, a refinement procedure that turns rejected candidates into stepping stones and retains and iteratively refines it using evidence accumulated across preceding attempts, delivering greater task-performance gains with fewer rollouts.

标题: PluginRSI: Recursive Improvement of Agent Harnesses with Reusable Plugins
S2_TLDR: This work introduces PluginRSI, which represents a harness as a composition of atomized plugins and organizes harness evolution around these plugins, and shows that accumulating reusable mechanisms provides an effective basis for continued harness improvement.

标题: HM-ROUTER: Joint Model and Harness Routing for Agentic Systems
S2_TLDR: HM-Router is introduced, a routing method that jointly selects a model and harness for each query, with an interaction term inspired by canonical polyadic tensor decomposition to capture how their compatibility varies with the query.

标题: RLHarness: Co-evolving Procedural Skills with Reinforcement Learning for Long-horizon Multimodal Reasoning
S2_TLDR: RLHARNESS is introduced, which organizes Skills, selection and execution protocols, few-shot demonstrations, and task contracts into a unified, versioned Harness and alternates Harness evolution with policy learning, showing that an evolving Harness complements RL by continually updating the external program that the policy learns to execute.

标题: Predict Before You Modify: Learning Improvement Dynamics for Self-Evolving Agents
S2_TLDR: P predictive self-evolution is introduced through an editable Improvement Dynamics Model (IDM), which outperforms HyperAgents across all four domains, and gains persist under matched token budgets that include both agent evolution and task evaluation, and extend to held-out tasks.

标题: Vestrum: Improving Agent Harnesses by Adapting Their Verification, Structure and Memory
S2_TLDR: V Vestrum, a framework that turns failures in execution traces into scoped harness changes without training the task model, is introduced, a framework that turns failures in execution traces into scoped harness changes without training the task model.

标题: AutoRef: Harness Optimization for Agentic Multi-Reference Image Generation
S2_TLDR: This work proposes AutoRef, which optimizes the harness automatically while keeping both models frozen: a coding agent iteratively rewrites the harness code, and discovers AutoRef-Harness, which improves the open-weight FLUX.

标题: Beyond Skill Evolution: Self-Evolving Context Management Policies for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses
S2_TLDR: ContextEvo, a framework that learns a context policy from long-horizon trajectories and reconstructs the model-visible context at key decision points, identifies context-related failures, and applies targeted policy updates, is introduced.

标题: EvoIn: Bridging Evolution and Internalization for Agent Fine-Tuning
S2_TLDR: EvoIn is an agent fine-tuning framework that bridges evolution and internalization, and consistently enables agents to learn stronger decision-making procedures, raising the pass rate by 10.9 points in-domain and by 9.2 points out-of-domain.

标题: Self-Evolving Harness on Multiple Tasks with the Agent as Its Own Optimizer
S2_TLDR: A framework close to recursive self-improvement is proposed: the same frozen model, on the same version of the harness, first solves tasks as the solver and then, as the proposer, reads the complete run records and directly edits the harness that runs it.

标题: Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning
S2_TLDR: Meta-reasoning, an inference-time harness that makes agentic meta-reasoning an explicit and structured reasoning process, keeps improving over the tested budget ranges where direct control plateaus, though its overhead can hurt at small budgets.

标题: Learning from Research: Toward Lifelong Agent Harness Evolution
S2_TLDR: This work introduces ScholarEvolve, a framework that automatically draws on state-of-the-art research to guide harness evolution and organizes the harness evolution directions into functional modules and uses topic modeling to identify distinct improvement strategies for each module.

标题: Turbo Harness: Instance-Adaptive Harness Optimization
S2_TLDR: This work introduces Turbo Harness, a framework that can adapt a globally optimized harness to each instance by reusing information generated during the original optimization process, and summarizes them into a structured playbook.

标题: MemCodex: Self-Programming Hierarchical Memory for Language Agents
S2_TLDR: This work introduces MemCodex, a self-evolving hierarchical memory system that organizes experience into executable memory programs for summaries, relational knowledge, reusable skills, and latent memory, and develops MemArena, a unified runtime that places heterogeneous data and memory systems behind a common interface.

标题: Growing an Agent/Prover Interface: Evolutionary Tool Design for Cost-Efficient Theorem Proving in Rocq and Lean
S2_TLDR: An evolutionary method where a frontier model incrementally proposes new features and only keeps the ones that improve the overall performance of smaller models is proposed, and the resulting server transfers to Lean, improving cost and time per solve on a subset of PutnamBench.

标题: GUI-HARVEST: Self-Improving GUI Agents through Evidence-Driven Harness Evolution
S2_TLDR: GUI-HARVEST is introduced, an automatic harness optimizer that enables self-improving GUI agents with frozen backbone models that outperforms Self-Harness and Meta-Harness, suggesting that GUI-specific diagnosis and validation help harness improvements generalize to unseen tasks.

标题: ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization
S2_TLDR: This work forms this missing dimension of harness optimization as an automated curriculum learning problem and introduces ActiveSaddler, which establishes automated curriculum learning as a new crucial optimization dimension for harness optimization.

标题: VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks
S2_TLDR: It is found that disagreement often exposes correct alternatives, while consensus can conceal errors, and verification skills can self-improve from failure feedback, demonstrating VeriHarness as a novel and critical approach for scaling long-horizon agentic verification.

标题: VERSE: Verified Self-Evolving Optimizer for Agent Harnesses
S2_TLDR: VersE, a Verified Self-Evolving optimizer for agent harnesses, improves all four evaluated harness optimizers on held-out SWE-rebench tasks and newer out-of-distribution tasks in five languages.

标题: Scaling Trajectories for Complex Tasks through Recursive Self-Rewrite
S2_TLDR: Recursive Self-Rewrite (RSR), a framework that uses one base model, Qwen-3.8-27B, to discover successful solutions under diverse harnesses and reconstruct them as training trajectories under a general harness, shows how diverse harness-assisted experiences can be reconstructed into reusable capabilities for a model operating under a general harness.

标题: MESH-Harness: Self-Improving Agent Harnesses via Bandit-Guided Compositional Evolution
S2_TLDR: Results show that combining module-level design reuse with feedback-driven compositional search can systematically improve agent harnesses while keeping overall optimization cost under control.

标题: Causal Improvement Graph for Agentic Harness Optimization
S2_TLDR: The Causal Improvement Graph (CIG) is introduced, a graph-governed meta-harness framework that externalizes the evolving improvement state in a persistent graph, allowing prior findings to directly govern subsequent Harness optimization through local proposer operations.

标题: HERA: Harness-Environment Co-Evolution for Reliable Agentic Abstention
S2_TLDR: HerA, a framework for harness-environment co-evolution for agentic abstention, is introduced, enabling smaller models to match the performance of more powerful models at an estimated 85% lower cost.

标题: EMHO: EMbodied Agent Harness Optimization via Experience Traces
S2_TLDR: Qualitative analysis shows that EMHO goes beyond recovering from failures and unproductive actions to reshape how the embodied agent interprets and interacts with its environment, and is evaluated on EmbodiedBench across navigation and manipulation tasks.

标题: CoTrace: Data Recipes for Training Terminal Agents with Harness-Model Co-Evolution
Safe, Persistent, and Evolving Agent Harness for Understanding Partially Observable Worlds
S2_TLDR: E-Ledger, a multi-agent harness for safe and persistent execution that employs a code approval layer that checks every proposed action against policy before execution, and maintains a world ledger of verified hidden rules alongside evidence-backed dynamic state is introduced.

标题: EvoBelief: Falsifiable World Models for Self-Improving LLM Agents
S2_TLDR: EvoBelief is introduced, a self-evolving world model that represents environment knowledge as falsifiable hypotheses that improves task performance and reuses learned rules across tasks, and demonstrates self-improvement through testable, revisable environment knowledge rather than model-parameter updates.

标题: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
S2_TLDR: Harness^2 is introduced, a plug-and-play, recursive agent harnessing framework that addresses two connected levels of recursion through two connected levels of recursion, enabling the agent to better adapt to future tasks.

标题: Cortex: Measurement-Gated Evolution and Pruning of Coding-Agent Skills and Rules
S2_TLDR: A tool that tests changes to the harness ofoding agents, a tool that saves fixes from the developer's sessions as replayable tasks, finds the corrections that recur, writes one skill or rule at a time, and keeps it only if repeated runs with and without it show a net gain and no task made noticeably worse.

标题: From Existing Methods to New Research Ideas: Two Perspectives on Recursive Self-Improvement
S2_TLDR: A unified taxonomy with nine design dimensions organized into four groups: update targets, update organization, update schedule and scope, feedback and selection is introduced, which places existing methods in a shared design space, where examining individual dimensions and their interactions can inspire new research ideas.

标题: Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses
S2_TLDR: Agentic Harness Engineering (AHE) is introduced, a closed loop that addresses harness engineering challenges through three matched observability pillars that turn every edit into a falsifiable contract, so harness evolution proceeds autonomously without collapsing into trial-and-error.

标题: Natural-Language Agent Harnesses
S2_TLDR: This paper introduces Natural-Language Agent Harnesses, editable documents that describe run-level harness policy, and Intelligent Harness Runtime (IHR), a shared runtime that interprets these documents into agent calls, handoffs, state updates, validation gates, and artifact contracts.

标题: Continual Harness: Online Adaptation for Self-Improving Foundation Agents
S2_TLDR: Continual Harness removes the human fully from this loop: a reset-free self-improving harness for embodied agents that formalizes and automates what was observed.

标题: Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit: Disentangling Evolution Capabilities in Self-Evolving LLM Agents
S2_TLDR: Investing capability budget in the task-solving agent rather than the evolver is suggested, and targeting harness invocation and long-horizon instruction following in agent training is suggested.

标题: HarnessForge: Joint Harness and Policy Evolution for Adaptive Agent Systems
S2_TLDR: Experiments show that HarnessForge consistently improves both Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B backbones, outperforming harness-only and policy-only baselines with gains of up to 12.0\% over the strongest baseline and achieving favorable rollout-efficiency tradeoffs, demonstrating that harness--policy co-evolution is effective and that executable compatibility between the harness and reasoning policy is essential for agent-system adaptation.

标题: SIA: Self Improving AI with Harness & Weight Updates
S2_TLDR: SIA is proposed, a self-improving loop in which a language-model agent (the Feedback-Agent) updates both the harness and the weights of a task-specific agent, which evaluates across three contrasting domains: Chinese legal charge classification, low-level GPU kernel optimisation, and single-cell RNA denoising.

标题: Adaptive Auto-Harness: Sustained Self-Improvement for Agentic System Deployment on Open-Ended Task Streams
S2_TLDR: Adaptive Auto-Harness is introduced, a framework and system for auto-harness that decomposes the gap to an oracle harness into evolution loss and adaptation loss and addresses these losses with a stateful multi-agent evolver, a harness tree with solve-time routing, and human-steering hooks for cases where history lacks the needed signal.

标题: VeRO: A Harness for Agents to Optimize Agents
S2_TLDR: This work introduces VeRO (Versioning, Rewards, and Observations), an outer harness that provides versioned snapshots, budget-controlled evaluation, and structured execution traces of target harnesses, and VeRO-Bench, a benchmark suite of target agents and tasks with reference evaluation procedures.

标题: Evolving Agents in the Dark: Retrospective Harness Optimization via Self-Preference
S2_TLDR: Retrospective Harness Optimization is introduced, a self-supervised method that optimizes the agent harness using only past trajectories and alters the agent's behavior patterns and sustains higher accuracy during long-horizon sessions.

标题: MemoHarness: Agent Harnesses That Learn from Experience
S2_TLDR: MemoHarness is introduced, an adaptive harness optimization framework that learns from its own executions and improves over the fixed harnesses it is compared against and shows selective transfer to unseen suites and base models.

标题: TTHE: Test-Time Harness Evolution
S2_TLDR: Test-Time Harness Evolution is introduced, which treats the executable harness as the state of test-time adaptation for LLM agents as evolution over executable control programs and identifies execution-derived proxy reliability as a central challenge for robust unsupervised agent improvement.

标题: Evo-Harness: Context-to-Harness Skill Compilation for Self-Evolving Agents
S2_TLDR: This formulation enables a systematic study of key self-improvement factors through the proposed Evo-Harness, and provides a principled understanding of how LLM agents can effectively learn on the fly.

标题: HARBOR: Automated Harness Optimization
S2_TLDR: This work argues that harness design is a first-class machine-learning problem and that automated configuration search dominates manual stacking once the flag space exceeds a handful of bits, and defends this claim in two steps.

标题: MOSS: Self-Evolution through Source-Level Rewriting in Autonomous Agent Systems

标题: DarwinX: Evolving Agent Harnesses Through Natural Selection

标题: OpenClaw-RL: Train Any Agent Simply by Talking

标题: Evo-Bench: Can Language Models Improve Agent Harness?

标题: HarnessEvolve: Learning from Reference Trajectories for Reliable Agent Self-Evolution
S2_TLDR: This paper introduces HarnessEvolve, a self-evolving framework that learns from reference trajectories to achieve reliable agent self-evolution, and overcomes credit assignment failure by generating reference trajectories and aligning failed executions against them to extract error signals.

标题: Harness-Aware Self-Evolving: Co-Evolving Model Weights, Harness, and Task Solutions

标题: Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable,Navigable, and Editable

标题: DREvo: Distilling Recalibrated Historical Experience for Harness Self-Evolution
S2_TLDR: A new harness self-evolution method, named DREvo, is proposed, which integrates function-level evidence anchoring, state-dependent evidence recalibration, and role-conditioned search intent distillation to determine which historical evidence remains valid and where the harness should evolve next.

标题: SafeHarness: Lifecycle-Integrated Security Architecture for LLM-based Agent Deployment
S2_TLDR: This paper introduces \safeharness{}, a security architecture in which four proposed defense layers are woven directly into the agent lifecycle to address above significant limitations: adversarial context filtering at input processing, tiered causal verification at decision making, privilege-separated tool control at action execution, and safe rollback with adaptive degradation at state update.

标题: The Meta-Agent Challenge: Are Current Agents Capable of Autonomous Agent Development?
S2_TLDR: The Meta-Agent Challenge (MAC) is introduced, an evaluation framework designed to test the capacity of frontier models for autonomous agent development, offering an empirical proxy for evaluating recursive self-improvement.

标题: SEAGym: An Evaluation Environment for Self-Evolving LLM Agents
S2_TLDR: SEAGym is introduced, an evaluation environment for measuring agent harness updates across training, validation, test, replay, and cost records, and the results show that frequent updates may fail to improve held-out performance, useful intermediate snapshots may collapse later, and source diversity and model backend can affect harness reliability.

标题: Living-Harness Is an Interactive-Agent Evolver
S2_TLDR: Living-Harness is proposed, a self-evolving agent harness that converts each completed trajectory and its evaluator signals into posterior evidence for bounded harness updates, and supports retrieval-only reuse of the evolved harness state across model backbones.

标题: AI4AI at Test-Time: Strong-to-Weak Capability Transfer via Harnesses
S2_TLDR: It is suggested that inference-time harness design is an important complement to conventional training-time distillation, enabling strong models to transfer cognitive structure to weaker models without retraining.

标题: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
S2_TLDR: Environment Harness is proposed, a programmable layer of plug-in components that wraps a static environment to reshape its behavior without modifying the underlying logic, enabling continuous, targeted co-evolution of the policy and its environment.

标题: Recursive self-improvement of AI research agents
S2_TLDR: AIDE^2, a system that implements this loop for a frontier AI research agent, shows that an AI research agent can improve its own research efficiency through recursive self-improvement, and that these gains transfer to tasks and domains the loop never encountered.

标题: EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

标题: LLMs Improving LLMs: Agentic Discovery for Test-Time Scaling

标题: Training with Harnesses: On-Policy Harness Self-Distillation for Complex Reasoning
S2_TLDR: OPHSD employs the harness-augmented current model as a teacher for self-distillation, thereby introducing extra supervisory signals from the harness beyond training data, yielding robust generalizability and strong standalone performance across diverse reasoning tasks.

标题: Autodata: An agentic data scientist to create high quality synthetic data
S2_TLDR: Autodata, a general method that enables AI agents to act as data scientists who build high quality training and evaluation data, is introduced and how to train such a data scientist agent is shown, so that it learns to create even stronger data.

标题: EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement
S2_TLDR: EvolveNet is introduced, a paradigm of collaborative harness evolution that moves experience extraction to the data and introduces scope-typed, evidence-guided program aggregation, which improves the shared harness in all five settings.

标题: Meta$^n$: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth

标题: Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents

标题: ClawEnvKit: Automatic Environment Generation for Claw-Like Agents
S2_TLDR: ClawEnvKit is introduced, an autonomous generation pipeline that instantiates this formalism from natural language descriptions and enables live evaluation: users describe a desired capability in natural language and obtain a verified environment on demand, turning evaluation into a continuous, user-driven process.

标题: Shepherd: Enabling Programmable Meta-Agents via Reversible Agentic Execution Traces

标题: Nautilus: From One Prompt to Plug-and-Play Robot Learning
S2_TLDR: NAUTILUS is an open-source harness that turns a single user prompt into ready-to-use reproduction, evaluation, fine-tuning, and deployment workflows, and aims to reduce the engineering burden of cross-family reproduction and evaluation in the ever-growing robot learning ecosystem.

标题: SkillsVote: Lifecycle Governance of Agent Skills from Collection, Recommendation to Evolution
S2_TLDR: SkillsVote is presented, a lifecycle-governance framework for Agent Skills across collection, recommendation, attribution, and evolution, that profiles a million-scale open source corpus for environment requirements, quality, and verifiability, and synthesizes tasks for verifiable skills.

标题: Towards Direct Evaluation of Harness Optimizers via Priority Ranking
S2_TLDR: This work presents a simple, low-cost design to directly evaluate harness optimizers, namely priority ranking, which quantifies optimizer ability at the step level without expensive rollouts or manual examination.

标题: SkillAdaptor: Self-Adapting Skills for LLM Agents from Trajectories

标题: HarnessBridge: Learnable Bidirectional Controller for LLM Agent Harness

标题: Evolution Fine-Tuning: Learning to Discover Across 371 Optimization Tasks
S2_TLDR: Evolution Fine-Tuning is introduced, a mid-training paradigm that teaches LLMs to evolve solutions across tasks by converting evolutionary search trajectories into supervision and serves as a "practice phase" for general-purpose discovery agents that do not solve new problems from scratch.

标题: HarnessMDP: Learning to Control LLM Agent Harnesses with Offline Reinforcement Learning
S2_TLDR: Extensive experiments on coding tasks, tau-bench, AgentBench, and other agent evaluation settings show that HarnessMDP consistently improves execution behavior and final task performance over baseline harnesses.

标题: When Does Continual Learning Require Learning

标题: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0

标题: Knowledge-Centric Self-Improvement
S2_TLDR: A new view of self-improving agentic systems: progress can be driven primarily by the curated persistent knowledge, which is contained in the knowledge rather than the agent, and improvement can be more inspectable, transferable, and portable.

标题: Auditing Harness Tampering in Self-Improving Agents

标题: EvoHarnessBench: Can Your Agents Keep Pace with an Evolving Harness?
S2_TLDR: EvoHarnessBench is introduced, a benchmark for evaluating agents under controlled harness evolution across three axes (tools, skills, and agents), and establishes harness evolution as a distinct challenge for building agents that can keep pace with an evolving harness while preserving previously effective behavior.

标题: Shepherd: A Runtime Substrate Empowering Meta-Agents with a Formalized Execution Trace
Bilevel Autoresearch: Meta-Autoresearching Itself

标题: SkillMOO: Multi-objective Optimization of Agent Skills for Software Engineering

标题: Federation over Text: Insight Sharing for Multi-Agent Reasoning

S2_TLDR: Findings show that harness provisioning follows a domain-dependent accuracy-cost Pareto frontier rather than a universal optimum, which means that in power grids, full provision remains accuracy-optimal, while map-based provisioning offers lower-cost alternatives.

S2_TLDR: HarnessRisk, a lifecycle oriented benchmark that organizes agent harness safety into six operational phases including Harness Configuration, Capability Extension, Runtime Operation, State Persistence, Action Control, and Incident Recovery, finds that explicit risk recognition does not reliably lead to safe action as some configurations detect risks in more than 90% of runs while retaining substantial attack success.

标题: StarHarness: Evolving Harnesses with Stratified Search for Enterprise Environments
S2_TLDR: StarHarness offers a practical way to reduce persistent model-environment mismatch in tool-rich enterprise tasks by stratifying tasks according to baseline failure behavior, separating proposer-visible search tasks from proposer-hidden selection tasks, and reserves held-out tasks for evaluating generalization.

标题: DataFoundry: Evolving Data Preparators via Recursive Self-Improvement
S2_TLDR: The DataFoundry is introduced, a framework for evolving data preparators through recursive self-improvement before large-scale data production, and it is found that recursively evolved preparators produce training data with higher downstream utility than baselines.

S2_TLDR: This paper proposes environment evolution, which incrementally increases environment difficulty off-policy and schedules the evolved environments generation by generation during training to provide continuous learning signals.

S2_TLDR: NeoHorse-1, a family of agent-native models developed to explore this path toward harness-mediated RSI through agentic post-training, provides an initial prototype of this feedback-driven process and a path toward harness-mediated RSI across successive iterations.

标题: Beyond the Model: Demystifying Harness Effects in Software Engineering Agents

Harness as an Asset: Enforcing Determinism via the Convergent AI Agent Framework (CAAF)

标题: ARIS: Autonomous Research via Adversarial Multi-Agent Collaboration

S2_TLDR: Mid-Harness is introduced, which samples and verifies candidate actions before forwarding one for execution, while keeping the generator and harness unchanged, and identifies action scaling as a promising target for test-time compute scaling in terminal agents.

标题: Cognitive Enhancement: Rethinking the Necessity of Role-Playing for Large Language Models
S2_TLDR: MLCP is proposed, a simple, training-free, and efficient multilingual prompt concatenation strategy that aggregates semantically equivalent role prompts to enrich complementary representational cues and consistently outperforms vanilla role-play prompting across all tested LLMs.

标题: ReLiveGym: Evaluating Long-Lived Agents over Weeks of Replayed Reality
S2_TLDR: This work introduces ReLiveGym, a diagnostic evaluation environment of long-lived tasks in which agents act sparsely over simulated weeks of chronologically replayed real-world news, market, and social-media streams and indicates model choice, action timing mechanism, and use of feedback as important considerations in the design of long-lived agents.

标题: Science or Slop?: Benchmarking and Mitigating Scientific Slop in AI-Generated Papers
S2_TLDR: SciSlopHarness is proposed, a harness-level framework that guides a fixed LLM to revise slop only where the experiment records support the change, and demonstrates that AI-generated scientific papers leave fundamental traces in their global reasoning, and that responsible mitigation demands strict evidentiary grounding rather than mere prose refinement.

标题: VideoEvolve: Evolving Agent Harnesses for Video Temporal Grounding
S2_TLDR: VideoEvolve is introduced, a framework that automatically evolves agent harnesses for video temporal grounding with a Cloze-Structured Harness Representation that preserves stage interfaces while leaving agent workflows and instructions open to evolution.

标题: Harness Annealing: Learning to Act with Less External Control
S2_TLDR: It is suggested that harness-supported experience can help reduce the runtime control required by a trained agent in language agents through objective harness internalization.

标题: WAMJET: A Harness for World Action Model Acceleration
S2_TLDR: WAMJET is an agentic harness that accelerates WAM inference by equipping coding agents with reusable optimization guidance and measurement and validation tools, and iteratively refines the acceleration stack as bottlenecks shift, while preserving action quality.

标题: A Design Theory for AI-Assisted Software Development Derived from Christopher Alexander's Theory of Form
S2_TLDR: A design theory derived from Christopher Alexander's theory of form, and a methodology for applying it, called Misfit-Governed Development (MGD), which addresses the generativity dimension of Alexander's 1996 OOPSLA challenge.

标题: HASTE: Evolving Agent Harnesses Against Emerging Attacks Using Sparse Evidence
S2_TLDR: HASTE is a multi-agent framework that evolves agent harnesses from sparse threat evidence through an adversarial interplay between safety-specification generation and attack-case generation, and consistently reduces attack success rates while preserving benign-task utility.

标题: Harness-Aware Distillation for Small Language Model Agents
S2_TLDR: HAD complements on-policy distillation with two components: an action preference that contrasts the same teacher's actions with and without the harness information, scored after the student's own reasoning, and a validity check that drops preference pairs whose preferred action contradicts the harness records.

标题: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Frontier Reasoning Data Synthesis
S2_TLDR: This work presents task-harness co-evolution, a framework for recursive harness self-improvement (RSI) in reasoning-data synthesis, and shows that combining both update schedules produces harder tasks than fixed-harness recursion or either schedule alone.

标题: ROAR: Unifying Runs across Heterogeneous AI-Driven Research Systems
S2_TLDR: ROAR is the first infrastructure designed to unify heterogeneous ADRS outputs through a relational schema and parsing layer that normalize heterogeneous ADRS outputs while preserving data lineage and temporal structure, and accommodating new systems without requiring schema modifications.

标题: Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time
S2_TLDR: It is argued that failure knowledge is conditional knowledge and should be conditionally exposed, and this principle is instantiated in Sentry, a failure-management layer that runs alongside the agent.

标题: Can LLM Agents Automate Reinforcement Learning for Text-to-Speech?

标题: AgentDiscover: Autonomous Discovery with Minimal Search Scaffolding

标题: Complex Agents, Shallow Tests: Demystifying and Enhancing Test Adequacy of Agent Harness in the Wild
S2_TLDR: This work conducts the first empirical study to systematically investigate the test adequacy of harness in real-world agentic systems and proposes HarnessTester, the first harness-oriented test generation technique that incorporates explicit agent-harness contract support to construct contract-faithful test setups and extensively exercise LDH code.

标题: Harness-Search: Guiding Long-Horizon Search through Multi-Agent Coordination
S2_TLDR: Harness-Search is introduced, a multi-agent search harness to reduce the local errors propagating across subsequent exploration, evidence curation, and termination decisions, and improves both retrieval and answer generation under the same policy backbone.

标题: What Does a Harness Repair? A Preregistered Study of Visibility, Baseline Adequacy and Evaluation Defects
S2_TLDR: A study of where harness search gains come from, with three small models, three benchmarks, replication and test partitions, a GEPA search arm and six evaluation defects injected one at a time, and all 47 primary endpoints.

标题: Harnessing LLMs with Direction-Scope Control for Combinatorial Solver Refinement
S2_TLDR: DiSH is introduced, a harness that jointly controls revision direction and scope that consistently improves QYI scores and reduces feasibility oscillation, while roughly halving feedback token consumption relative to prior methods that use full feedback.

标题: What May an Agent Change About Itself? A Containment Floor for Self-Configuring Agent Runtimes
S2_TLDR: A rule is proposed: the agent may change fields that grant abilities, and may never change fields that set its limits, which is enforced as a containment floor inside the configuration tool and measured what happens with and without it.

标题: VERA: Scaling Verifiable Environments for Agentic co-Evolution
S2_TLDR: This work presents VERA, which builds precise and verifiable environments at scale and lets agents evolve on them, and creates a verifier which gates model checkpoints and harness edits using explicit development-set acceptance criteria.

标题: Stateless Language Agents: Scaling Long-Horizon Automated Research
S2_TLDR: This work introduces Stateless Language Agents (SLAs), built on the principle of stateful search with stateless agents, and evaluates SLA against three recent frameworks on software engineering, kernel optimization, and algorithm design at budgets of up to one billion tokens.

标题: Agent Plasticity: Measuring Self-Improvement Through Experience
S2_TLDR: This work introduces agent plasticity, the efficiency with which an agent converts experience into gains in future held-out performance, and studies self-improvement in a controlled setting where agents amortize past experience into reusable artifacts that are inherited by future instances.

标题: PhysEvo: Astra Can Act, Let It
S2_TLDR: PhysEvo turns the consequences of action into persistent, testable changes to how a frozen model acts and improves, and turns the consequences of action into persistent, testable changes to how a frozen model acts and improves.

标题: HarnessSecurity-Bench: Do Security Mechanisms Really Protect Coding Agent Harnesses?
S2_TLDR: This work presents HarnessSecurity, the first systematic empirical study and benchmark of open- and closed-source coding agent harnesses, and derives a ten-mechanism taxonomy and assesses 400 harness-mechanism cells using independent ratings by researchers and large language model judges.

标题: From Pareto to Preference: Personalized Test-Time Scaling via Amortized Agentic Policy Discovery
S2_TLDR: PersonTTS is proposed, an amortized agentic policy-discovery framework that reuses prior search experience through requirement-matched controller initialization and source-distilled procedural guidance, while retaining target-profile evaluation for every candidate.

标题: Verification and Self-Improvement in Agentic AI: Foundations and Limits
S2_TLDR: It is proved that independent majority amplification preserves both languages, whereas existential acceptance over random tapes can admit incorrect outputs, under a uniform pointwise probability gap and task-relative soundness.

标题: DuplexAgent-RSI: Recursive Harness Improvement for Full-Duplex Voice Agent Collaboration
S2_TLDR: Experiments on intelligence, agentic, and duplex benchmarks show that DuplexAgent combines continuous interaction with difficult reasoning and complex task execution, achieving stronger spoken-knowledge and executable-tool scores than the compared delegated systems while maintaining strong interruption response.

标题: TestPrism: Rethinking Test Evaluation Beyond a Single Reference
S2_TLDR: TestHelix is introduced, which combines heterogeneous synthesis of test and repair pairs with peer cross validation and recursive self improvement (RSI), which improves Joint Success Function by 8.67 to 9.00 percentage points over the native harness comparators in the TestHelix evaluation.

标题: Recurrent Harness for Agentic Continual Learning
S2_TLDR: ReHarness is proposed, a recurrent harness framework for agentic continual learning that complements forward read and write with backward revision under a strictly online streaming protocol and consistently outperforms strong raw-context baselines, memory- and reflection-based methods, and prompt optimization approaches.

标题: Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling: When Weight Training Should Begin

标题: Tracing the Thoughts of a Coding Agent Playing ARC-AGI-3: Lessons for Continual Learning

标题: Evo$^2$: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution
S2_TLDR: This work proposes Evo$^2, a framework for weight-harness co-evolution that significantly outperforms existing self-evolution methods and demonstrates the applicability of the framework Evo$^2$ across domains and its broad transferability across models and tasks.

标题: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
S2_TLDR: Through extensive experiments across web search, web navigation, and deep research benchmarks, it is shown that Web\$hell achieves strong task performance at lower cost, and the results further indicate the importance of interface design for effective web access.

标题: AgentSWE: Can Coding Agents Build the Agent You Actually Want?
S2_TLDR: AgentSWE is introduced, a benchmark for agent software engineering spanning three stages of the agent development lifecycle: Creation of a complete agent from a natural-language requirement, Editing of production agent codebases, and Optimization toward a measurable target.

标题: RegulaTutor: A Theory-Informed Framework for Long-Term Personalized Learning
S2_TLDR: RegulaTutor is introduced, a theory-informed framework for long-term personalized tutoring that connects historical evidence, learner interpretation, and learner-facing instruction that improves historical-evidence accuracy, learner diagnosis, and judged teaching quality on average across evaluated model configurations.

标题: AutoEnvScaling: Automating the Data Flywheel with Terminal Agents
S2_TLDR: AutoEnvScaling is introduced, which treats environment design as a terminal task and uses agents to automate the data flywheel and enable recursive self-improvement (RSI), and shows a path toward agents building their own training environments, reducing human reliance and taking a core step toward RSI.

标题: LongHarness: Advancing Agentic Reasoning over 100M-Token Corpora via Stateful Evidence Management
S2_TLDR: LongHarness is presented, a model-agnostic harness that makes the interaction between acquired evidence and evolving conclusions explicit and uses unresolved conclusions to guide exploration toward missing information, while newly acquired evidence strengthens or revises the conclusions that directed the search.

标题: Reasoning Is More Than the Model: Harness-Aware Evaluation of Agents on Verifiable Reasoning Tasks
S2_TLDR: AlphaDiana moves agent evaluation beyond asking whether a system succeeds toward explaining why a model-harness system succeeds or fails, and standardizes models, harnesses, benchmarks, execution environments, scorers, budgets, and trajectory logging, enabling controlled comparisons across both models and harnesses.

标题: Workflow, Not Prose: A Multi-Agent Methodology for Data Agents
S2_TLDR: Two methodology contributions are presented: a declarative-markdown harness with a small mutation surface, and an auto-research loop in which failure-mode analysis on completed experiments proposes new hypotheses, optionally human-reviewed, that progress through the same experiment workflow.

标题: Toward Self-Evolving Data Agents for Autonomous Data Analysis
S2_TLDR: Comparisons against stronger model and coding-agent competitors further indicate that both domain-specific agent runtime structure and foundation-model strength matter for autonomous data analysis.

标题: GRPO Didn’t Pass the Bar (But the Harness Did): Harness-Guided Post-Training for Legal Agents
S2_TLDR: How much of a legal harness’s procedural advantage can be internalized back into the base model's weights, so the model’s performance improves even under a plain default harness at inference?
